description:
## Goal

Wire agent-manager's run executor and workspace-sandbox's apply path to the locked auditability contract so sandboxing is the seamless, audit-by-default execution path for coding runs.

## Locked contract reference

See `scenarios/swarm-manager/research/agent-sandbox-auditability-contract/conclusion.md` Findings 1-3 and the mirror at `scenarios/workspace-sandbox/docs/AUDITABILITY_CONTRACT.md`.

## Locked defaults to encode

| Lever | Default |
|---|---|
| `mode` | `tracking` (`protected` is reserved; requesting it errors until its implementation lands) |
| `manualReview` | `false` (opt-in only) |
| `autoApply` | `true` |
| `applyOnFailure` | `true` |
| `lock` | `false` |
| `networkMode` | `localhost` (supports `none|localhost|full`) |
| `sandboxCreation` | eager (sandbox created at run start regardless of whether the agent writes anything) |
| Agent-side awareness | none (no prompt or behavior changes based on sandbox mode) |

## Apply timing state machine

- `manualReview=false` (default): in-acceptance changes auto-apply at run end; out-of-acceptance changes are persisted as `state=pending-review` provenance and remain in the sandbox.
- `manualReview=true` (opt-in): NO apply at run end; all changes persist as `state=pending-review`. The sandbox itself MUST persist beyond run end until the operator approves or denies. Approval can come from any of three surfaces (git-control-tower AI Changes, agent-manager run-detail diff, workspace-sandbox sandbox-detail diff); the originating surface is recorded on the resulting state transition for audit.
- Apply behavior is identical regardless of run outcome (`runOutcome` in {success, failure, cancelled, timeout} is captured on the provenance record but does not gate apply). Failed runs that produced changes still write provenance and still auto-apply (subject to acceptance).

## Provenance writes (depends on Action 5 / GCT schema work)

Every applied or pending-review file MUST carry:
- `agent_manager_run_id`, `conversation_id`, `cost`, and execution metadata at the run-group level.
- `runOutcome` in {success, failure, cancelled, timeout} on `ProvenanceRunGroup`.
- `state` in {applied, pending-review, denied} on each `ProvenanceFile` (per-file, not per-run, so a single run can mix in-acceptance and out-of-acceptance edits without splitting the run group).

Workspace-sandbox owns state transitions; this item is the writer side.

## Required surface changes

1. Agent-manager run executor (`scenarios/agent-manager/api/internal/orchestration/run_executor.go`) creates a sandbox EAGERLY at run start, injects `VROOLI_SANDBOX_ID`, `VROOLI_SANDBOX_MERGED`, `VROOLI_SANDBOX_SCOPE`, and calls workspace-sandbox Apply at run end when `manualReview=false`.
2. Per-run config surface accepts `mode`, `manualReview`, `autoApply`, `applyOnFailure`, `lock`, `networkMode`, `acceptanceAllow`, `acceptanceDeny`. None pass through to the agent prompt.
3. Naming alignment: `RequiresApproval` at the toolregistry level is preserved for canonical-repo-modifying tools that bypass the sandbox (e.g., direct git commit). It is NOT wired to general apply behavior. New per-run levers use `manualReview` / `autoApply` / `applyOnFailure` names.
4. No-op runs still produce an empty provenance record (eager creation contract).

## Expected deliverables

1. Run executor changes implementing eager sandbox creation, run-end apply for `manualReview=false`, and persistence-beyond-run-end for `manualReview=true`.
2. Per-run config surface and defaults wired through to workspace-sandbox API calls.
3. Provenance writes populating `runOutcome` (run group) and per-file `state` (depends on `execute/gct-pending-ai-provenance-hardening` schema landing first or in parallel).
4. Tests covering: success run + auto-apply, failure run + auto-apply, partial-acceptance split (in-acceptance applied + out-of-acceptance pending-review on same run), `manualReview=true` deferred apply with sandbox persistence, and no-op run empty-provenance.
5. Documentation note pointing future contributors to the AUDITABILITY_CONTRACT.md.

## Open detail for implementer

The garbage-collection rule for abandoned `manualReview=true` sandboxes (TTL or operator-action timeout) is intentionally left to this item to specify, not pre-decided in the contract. Pick a rule, document it, and add coverage.

## Key references

- `scenarios/agent-manager/api/internal/orchestration/run_executor_test.go`
